_comment: Read-only validation shared by the Python and TypeScript suites. 'reject' must fail validate_query/validateQuery with writes disabled; 'allow' must pass. Validation is a keyword check, so it errs on the side of rejecting.
reject: WITH u AS (UPDATE orders SET status = 'x' RETURNING 1) SELECT 1
WITH d AS (DELETE FROM orders RETURNING *) SELECT count(*) FROM d
WITH i AS (INSERT INTO t VALUES (1) RETURNING 1) SELECT 1
SELECT email INTO TEMP shadow FROM customers
MERGE INTO t USING s ON t.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE
DO $$ BEGIN EXECUTE 'DROP TABLE t'; END $$
SELECT 'a'''; UPDATE t SET a = 1; SELECT ''''
SELECT E'\''; UPDATE t SET a = 1; SELECT '1'
SELECT name'x'; UPDATE t SET a = 1; SELECT 'y'
SELECT "a"""; UPDATE t SET a = 1; SELECT "b"
SELECT a$b$ FROM t; UPDATE t SET a = 1; SELECT $b$
allow: WITH c AS (SELECT * FROM customers) SELECT * FROM c
SELECT * FROM todo WHERE done = false
SELECT * FROM audit WHERE action IN ('INSERT', 'DELETE')
SELECT * FROM posts WHERE title ILIKE '%into%'
SELECT * FROM t WHERE note = 'it''s an update'
